mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3.0% signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 3.0%, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 5.0% signals tightening labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy and suppressing equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 5.0%, or the mean return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction starts above 2000 thousand units signals strong housing demand and rising consumer confidence, which drives equity market optimism and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances when HOUST exceeds 2000, or the average return in such periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production below 119.0 index points signals weakening manufacturing activity and economic contraction, which triggers risk-off sentiment and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates negative 20-day returns in less than 40% of periods when INDPRO falls below 119.0, or the average return in such periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in both real personal consumption expenditures and residential construction signals broad-based demand strength, which drives corporate earnings optimism and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in less than 40% of instances where both GDPC1 and HOUST are rising, or the joint signal has a Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in CPI and a decline in the federal funds rate signals disinflationary pressures and an accommodative monetary stance, which boosts equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases > 0.2% MoM and FEDFUNDS decreases > 0.1pp
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 5-day returns in less than 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL rises >0.2% MoM and FEDFUNDS falls >0.1pp, or the interaction signal has a Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in non-farm payroll growth signals a labor market that is both tightening and expanding, which increases inflation expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in less than 40% of instances where UNRATE falls >0.2pp and PAYEMS rises >50k, or the interaction signal has a Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures above 11090 billion dollars signals strong aggregate demand, which drives corporate revenue growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in less than 40% of periods when GDPC1 exceeds 11090, or the average return in such periods is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
